txt: IF a format reader receives hostile or malformed input, THEN the reader SHALL return a clean error, never panicking, over-allocating or returning a wrong tensor with a nil error.

The length, dimension and nesting claim read from a file header SHALL be capped before any allocation, with header size, element count and array depth bounded (depth at most 64) and growth never pre-allocated from a claimed size.

The a shape product computed from untrusted dimensions SHALL use the division-before-multiply overflow guard and reject negative dimensions, since a post-multiply cap wraps and lets a hostile header through.
The fuzz target SHALL reach the parser it names, taking raw inner bytes rather than a container envelope.

ti: Cut the residual serial cost in gguf ReadFile
Pre-size and then mmap the gguf data-section read
Eliminate the bounds checks and unhoisted scale products in the Q4_K and Q6_K dequant loops
Make gguf ReadRaw subslice instead of copying every tensor

note:
Both halves landed and measured.

Q4_K: dequantQ4_KInto reslices to fixed lengths (raw[o:o+q4kBlockSize], dst[base:base+64]) instead of the open-ended form. MEASURED 177,736 -> 154,195 ns on BenchmarkDequantQ4_K, 1.15x. The per-element IsInBounds at q4k.go:75:8 and :76:8 are gone, replaced by one IsSliceInBounds per sub-block — N per-element checks traded for one per-run check. Bit-identity structural: no arithmetic expression changed, y[l] addresses the same element as dst[base+l] by construction.

Q6_K: the four scale products were recomputed on every one of 32 iterations to produce 8 distinct values per 128-element group, because is := l / 16 takes only two values. Split the loop at that boundary and hoisted them, plus the same fixed-length reslicing. MEASURED 230,684 -> 178,457 ns on BenchmarkDequantQ6_K, 1.29x, and IsInBounds in the loop body drops to zero.

BIT-IDENTITY, the part that mattered: Q6_K touches arithmetic GROUPING, so the structural argument used for Q4_K does not carry. The original d * float32(int8(sc[...])) * float32(q-32) associates left-to-right as (d*sc)*(q-32); hoisting s := d*sc and writing s*(q-32) reproduces that grouping exactly, whereas folding the other way as d*(sc*(q-32)) would not. That argument was VERIFIED rather than trusted: the raw output bits were captured for a deterministic 7-block input before and after (7,168 bytes) and compared byte-for-byte — identical. The capture harness was removed afterwards; the existing golden, round-trip, hostile-input and fuzz suites remain the standing gates and all pass.

Both A/Bs used an interleaved three-round file-copy toggle on the same host in one session, medians reported — after an earlier non-interleaved comparison on a different task was shown to be unreliable by a control benchmark that moved 20 percent with no code change.

CORRECTION carried forward from the original brief: it claimed q5k.go and q2k.go compile bounds-check-free and could serve as the clean comparison. They do NOT — a check_bce dump reports 29 findings across those two files. Their idiom is still the right model for the inner store loop, but the blanket claim is wrong.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the NEON/SIMD dequant kernels the brief listed as a follow-on. Both fixes here are the correct precursor — with the scales hoisted the Q6_K inner loop is a pure vmul over 16 lanes — but the vectorization itself is a separate, larger change needing its own arch-gated parity work, and it belongs with the arm64 SIMD tasks rather than here. No perfscan rule was minted for this pattern: the loop-invariant-per-stride shape is already specified in the reduce/odometer detector task, and duplicating it here would create two rules for one anti-pattern.

ti: Benchmark Q2_K/Q3_K/Q5_K single-token QMatMul before fusing them

note:
DONE, all three fused. Q2_K 1.67x (959.1-965.4us -> 571.2-586.3us), Q3_K 1.75x (1092.5-1103.6us -> 617.7-646.8us), Q5_K 1.41x (794.0-796.6us -> 560.7-570.2us). Interleaved, 4 alternations per quant, one quant at a time, every arm inside 5%. All seven quant types now sit at 102 allocs per decode step; the span across formats collapsed from 525-1082us to 528-626us.

THE TASK'S CAUTION WAS RIGHT TO DEMAND A MEASUREMENT AND WRONG ABOUT THE DIRECTION. It argued the aggressive quants might not repay fusion the way the deployment formats did, because they do more per-element unpacking. They repaid it MORE (1.41-1.75x against 1.40-1.52x). The alloc signature the task said to check first — 107 vs 102 per decode step — was present on all three and was the correct predictor; the reasoning about unpacking cost was not.

PS6003 FALSE-POSITIVED ON THE FIRST DRAFT AND THE CODE WAS CHANGED, NOT THE RULE. Wrapping a dispatch switch in a single `if m == 1` guard hides the covered set behind a function value the AST check cannot follow, so it reported a gap that no longer existed. Naming the five types in the guard keeps coverage legible to the check and meaningful for whoever adds an eighth type. Teaching the rule dataflow would have cost soundness and bought nothing. Second time this campaign that dogfooding PS6003 on fresh code corrected something — the first was its own || handling.

GATE: the three paths were added to TestQMatMulFusedDecodeMatchesGeneralPathExactly before being written. Four mutations turn it red (sign-flipped Q2_K dmin offset, wrong Q2_K activation group, inverted Q3_K high-bit select, Q5_K fifth bit shifted one position) while every pre-existing 1e-5 test stays green. Three further probes were REJECTED as invalid rather than counted: two anchors matched both a dequant and its fused twin, one did not compile.

LANDED: commit 621f4b68. Learning in PERF-FASTPATH-FAMILY-001 and NUM-ACCUM-NARROW-001; research R-01KYMVGRENEND is now fully consumed. NOT DONE, deliberately: no fusion for m>1 (it would re-dequantize per activation row), and no SIMD or integer-accumulator rewrite of any dot — that trades the bit-identity these gates rest on.
